native_calibration.basis: Native MD comparative calibration: tank_nsb_armor_upgrade adds 7.5% armour per level and costs speed/reliability; tank_nsb_engine_upgrade adds 3.5% speed per level and costs reliability/fuel/IC. am_hai_m101.name: M2A1 105 mm Howitzer

historical_specs.notes: Conventional 105 mm M2A1/M101 family. Native early towed artillery is non-modular.

notes: The CIA February 20, 1969 Haitian inventory explicitly records US 105 mm howitzers. The standard M2/M101 family is the conservative representative fixed equipment model; precise Haitian serials and ammunition subtypes are not asserted.
Native fixed towed-artillery equipment has no module designer. No self-propelled chassis, autoloader or later gun system is invented.

am_jam_bell47.name: Bell 47G-3B-1

historical_specs.notes: Original light utility helicopter; unarmed cabin. No later turbine JetRanger, Bell 212 or armed helicopter capability.

notes: Jamaica Air Wing history dates the first Bell 47 to October 1963; airframe records identify H-1 serial 2901 and H-2 serial 2907. The official unit history is currently intermittently unavailable; the service narrative and airframe register corroborate the date.

am_guy_landrover.name: Land Rover (unarmored utility)

historical_specs.notes: Conventional British military 4x4 utility family. The CIA inventory does not establish an exact individual Series II/IIA serial or body specification.

notes: The CIA inventory dates UK Land Rover quarter-ton transports to 1966 and separately lists armored Land Rover vehicles acquired in 1967. This design represents only the unarmored utility vehicles; it does not turn the Shorland into a modern APC.

method: Representative service designs supported by pre-1970 operator evidence. Imports record original producer and do not transfer complete industrial packages. Empty arrays are explicitly unassigned or unevidenced packages, not absence of basic arms. No equipment, ships, aircraft, units or stockpiles are spawned.
